text:
ConocoPhillips gained 0.4% today to close at $129.84, continuing a steady climb over the past week as oil prices have found support despite recent volatility. The move reflects a tug-of-war in the oil market: while crude has fallen modestly on news that the IEA and G7 are releasing diesel stockpiles to ease supply pressures, the global diesel shortage remains acute — with shipping costs to China running 10 times pre-war rates and U.S. heating oil prices up sharply heading into winter. For an integrated oil producer like ConocoPhillips, tighter fuel markets and elevated geopolitical risk (Persian Gulf tanker attacks) still underpin stronger margins, even as politicians and the IEA try to cap prices.

The stock's 1.4% gain over two weeks sits in a broader context of oil supply anxiety that hasn't really been resolved. The gap between U.S. crude ($96/barrel) and world oil ($125/barrel) is unusually wide, signaling regional supply strains that emergency releases can only partly address — and that environment typically supports upstream producers' earnings power over the coming months.
